draft.title: Scaling area and volume
card: When every length of a shape or solid is multiplied by k, the new shape is similar to the old one. Here k is the scale factor for lengths.
area scales by k². Area is length × length, so both lengths are multiplied by k. Example: k = 3 makes every area 9 times as large.
volume scales by k³. Volume is length × length × length, so three lengths are multiplied by k. Example: k = 2 makes every volume 8 times as large.
To find k from areas or volumes, go backwards. If the area ratio is 25, then k = √25 = 5. If the volume ratio is 27, then k = ∛27 = 3.
draft.remember: Lengths × k, areas × k², volumes × k³.

a.q: A small tin has a base area of 12 cm². A larger similar tin has all lengths 3 times as long. What is the base area of the larger tin?
a.why: Area scales by k² = 3² = 9, so the base area is 12 × 9 = 108 cm². Multiplying by 3 gives 36 cm², which scales the area as if it were a length.
a.clue: Area is length × length, so k is used twice.

b.q: Two similar water tanks hold 40 L and 320 L. The small tank is 50 cm tall. How tall is the large tank?
b.why: The volume ratio is 320 ÷ 40 = 8, so k³ = 8 and k = 2. The height is 50 × 2 = 100 cm. Using 8 as the length factor gives 400 cm, which forgets that volume scales by k³.
b.clue: Find k by going backwards from the volume ratio.
